claim: IL-6 plays an important role in determining the fate of effector CD4 cells and the cytokines that these cells produce.
source: IL-6 plays an important role in determining the fate of effector CD4 cells and the cytokines that these cells produce.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about IL-6 function, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: IL-6-dependent signal facilitates the formation of mitochondrial respiratory chain supercomplexes to sustain high mitochondrial membrane potential late during activation of CD4 cells.
source: IL-6-dependent signal facilitates the formation of mitochondrial respiratory chain supercomplexes to sustain high mitochondrial membrane potential late during activation of CD4 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D demonstrating increased supercomplexes in IL-6-treated cells.

claim: Mitochondrial hyperpolarization caused by IL-6 is uncoupled from the production of ATP by oxidative phosphorylation.
source: Mitochondrial hyperpolarization caused by IL-6 is uncoupled from the production of ATP by oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing no difference in ATP levels or oxygen consumption rates despite increased MMP.

claim: Increased mitochondrial membrane potential by IL-6 is a mechanism to raise the levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ late during activation of CD4 cells.
source: However, it is a mechanism to raise the levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ late during activation of CD4 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing increased mitochondrial Ca2+ in IL-6-treated cells.

claim: Increased levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ in the presence of IL-6 are used to prolong Il4 and Il21 expression in effector CD4 cells.
source: Increased levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ in the presence of IL-6 are used to prolong Il4 and Il21 expression in effector CD4 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing that inhibiting mitochondrial Ca2+ reduces IL-4 and IL-21 production.

claim: The effect of IL-6 on mitochondrial membrane potential and mitochondrial Ca2+ is an alternative pathway by which IL-6 regulates effector function of CD4 cells.
source: Thus, the effect of IL-6 on mitochondrial membrane potential and mitochondrial Ca2+ is an alternative pathway by which IL-6 regulates effector function of CD4 cells and it could contribute to the pathogenesis of inflammatory diseases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Inhibition of IL-6 signaling by an anti-IL-6R antibody has been shown to be a highly effective therapy in treating patients with RA.
source: Inhibition of IL-6 signaling by an anti-IL-6R antibody has been shown to be a highly effective therapy in treating patients with RA (Tanaka and Kishimoto, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tanaka and Kishimoto, 2012.

claim: IL-6 enhances Th2 differentiation through an auto-feedback loop by upregulating autocrine IL-4 production.
source: It enhances Th2 differentiation through an auto-feedback loop by upregulating autocrine IL-4 production (Rincon et al., 1997; Diehl et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rincon et al., 1997 and Diehl et al., 2002.

claim: IL-6 inhibits IFNγ production and Th1 differentiation.
source: IL-6 inhibits IFNγ production and Th1 differentiation (Diehl et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Diehl et al., 2000.

claim: In combination with TGFβ, IL-6 contributes to the differentiation of Th17 cells.
source: In combination with TGFβ, IL-6 also contributes to the differentiation of Th17 cells (Bettelli et al., 2006; Ivanov et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bettelli et al., 2006; Ivanov et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2007.

claim: IL-6 inhibits regulatory T cell function and downregulates Foxp3 expression.
source: IL-6 inhibits regulatory T cell function and downregulates Foxp3 expression (Pasare and Medzhitov, 2003; Dienz and Rincon, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pasare and Medzhitov, 2003 and Dienz and Rincon, 2009.

claim: IL-6 alone, without the need of TGFβ, induces IL-21 expression, a mechanism by which it promotes the generation of follicular T helper (Tfh) cells.
source: In addition, IL-6 alone, without the need of TGFβ, induces IL-21 expression, a mechanism by which it promotes the generation of follicular T helper (Tfh) cells (Nurieva et al., 2008; Suto et al., 2008; Dienz et al., 2009; Diehl et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nurieva et al., 2008; Suto et al., 2008; Dienz et al., 2009; Diehl et al., 2012.

claim: Most freshly isolated CD4 cells were hyperpolarized as shown by high TMRE staining.
source: Most freshly isolated CD4 cells were hyperpolarized as shown by the high TMRE staining (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cells activated in the absence of IL-6 depolarized progressively during activation.
source: However, cells activated in the absence of IL-6 depolarized progressively during activation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The presence of IL-6 prevents mitochondrial depolarization during CD4 cell activation.
source: Interestingly, the presence of IL-6 prevents mitochondrial depolarization during CD4 cell activation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: After 48hr of activation, most CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 maintained a high MMP (TMREhigh).
source: After 48hr of activation, most CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 maintained a high MMP (TMREhigh) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The presence of exogenous IL-2 did not affect MMP in activated CD4 cells.
source: In contrast to IL-6, the presence of exogenous IL-2, the main growth factor of T cells, did not affect MMP in activated CD4 cells (Figure 1C), supporting a selective role for IL-6 on MMP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: IL-6 did not affect the overall mitochondrial mass as determined by the levels of COX IV, NDUFS3 and NDUFA9.
source: IL-6 did not affect the overall mitochondrial mass as determined by the levels of COX IV (Complex IV subunit of ETC), NDUFS3 and NDUFA9 (Complex I subunits) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The frequency of live cells among those activated in the presence of IL-6 was not significantly different from the frequency of live cells in the absence of IL-6.
source: In addition, the frequency of live cells among those activated in the presence of IL-6 was not significantly different from the frequency of live cells in the absence of IL-6 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The increase of MMP triggered by IL-6 is not a consequence of survival or change in mitochondrial mass.
source: Thus, the increase of MMP triggered by IL-6 is not a consequence of survival or change in mitochondrial mass.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing no difference in cell viability or mitochondrial mass markers.

claim: A large frequency of OT-II CD4 cells activated with WT APC showed a high MMP.
source: Similar to CD4 cells activated with anti-CD3/CD28 Abs in the presence of IL-6, a large frequency of OT-II CD4 cells activated with WT APC showed a high MMP (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and 1G.

claim: A blocking anti-IL-6 Ab drastically decreased the frequency of cells with high MMP when OT-II cells were activated with WT APCs.
source: However, a blocking anti-IL-6 Ab drastically decreased the frequency of cells with high MMP (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and 1G.

claim: Very low frequency of activated CD4 cells showed high MMP when APC from IL-6 KO mice were used.
source: In contrast to WT APCs, very low frequency of activated CD4 cells showed high MMP when APC from IL-6 KO mice were used (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and 1G.

claim: Addition of exogenous IL-6 to cells activated with IL-6 KO APCs restored high MMP.
source: Remarkably, addition of exogenous IL-6 to cells activated with IL-6 KO APCs restored high MMP (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and 1G.

claim: IL-6 derived from APC during in vitro activation of CD4 cells is essential to maintain mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
source: Thus, these results indicate that IL-6 derived from APC during in vitro activation of CD4 cells is essential to maintain mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing the effects of IL-6 KO APCs and blocking antibodies.

claim: The fraction of OT-II cells maintaining a high MMP was significantly greater in WT mice relative to IL-6 KO mice after in vivo immunization.
source: Similar to in vitro results, the fraction of OT-II cells maintaining a high MMP was significantly greater in WT mice relative to IL-6 KO mice (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H from in vivo experiments.

claim: IL-6 plays an essential role in maintaining the MMP during activation of CD4 cells.
source: Together, these results indicate that IL-6 plays an essential role in maintaining the MMP during activation of CD4 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results presented in Figure 1.

claim: Mitochondrial cristae shape has been shown to influence the efficiency of the respiratory chain in part by affecting the formation of respiratory chain supercomplexes.
source: Mitochondrial cristae shape has been shown to influence the efficiency of the respiratory chain in part by affecting the formation of respiratory chain supercomplexes (RCS) (Hackenbrock, 1966; Gomes et al., 2011; Cogliati et al., 2013), formed of Complex I together with Complex III and Complex IV.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hackenbrock, 1966; Gomes et al., 2011; Cogliati et al., 2013.

claim: The function of RCS is to facilitate the transfer of electrons between complexes and increase Complex I activity while reducing the electron leak from ETC and mitigate the production of reactive oxygen species.
source: The function of RCS is to facilitate the transfer of electrons between complexes and increase Complex I activity while reducing the electron leak from ETC and mitigate the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS) (Schägger, 1995; Acín-Pérez et al., 2008; Althoff et al., 2011; Winge, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Schägger, 1995; Acín-Pérez et al., 2008; Althoff et al., 2011; Winge, 2012.

claim: No obvious differences in mitochondrial integrity or mitochondrial mass were observed in cells activated with or without IL-6.
source: No obvious differences in mitochondrial integrity or mitochondrial mass were observed in cells activated with or without IL-6 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was no increase in the number of mitochondria in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6.
source: Similarly, there was no increase in the number of mitochondria in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The morphology of the mitochondrial cristae in cells activated with IL-6 was different from that of cells activated without IL-6.
source: However, the morphology of the mitochondrial cristae in cells activated with IL-6 was different from that of cells activated without IL-6 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The number of mitochondria with expanded and disorganized cristae was greater in CD4 cells activated in the absence of IL-6 compared with CD4 cells activated with IL-6.
source: The number of mitochondria with expanded and disorganized cristae was greater in CD4 cells activated in the absence of IL-6 compared with CD4 cells activated with IL-6 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TEM data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The number of mitochondria with tight and organized cristae was higher in cells activated in the presence of IL-6.
source: In contrast, the number of mitochondria with tight and organized cristae was higher in cells activated in the presence of IL-6 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TEM data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: IL-6 affects mitochondrial cristae shape during activation of CD4 cells.
source: Thus, IL-6 affects mitochondrial cristae shape during activation of CD4 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TEM data showing differences in cristae morphology.

claim: The levels of RCS but not the levels of individual Complex I or Complex III were increased in mitochondria from IL-6-stimulated CD4 cells.
source: The levels of RCS but not the levels of individual Complex I or Complex III were increased in mitochondria from IL-6-stimulated CD4 cells, as determined by the presence of NDUFA9 (Complex I) and Core I (Complex III) within the RCS region (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by BN-PAGE Western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Despite the increased MMP, IL-6 reduced the production of mROS.
source: Despite the increased MMP, IL-6 reduced the production of mROS (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by MitoSOX flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: The formation of RCS facilitated by IL-6 makes possible for this cytokine to sustain mitochondria hyperpolarization while minimizing the production of mROS during activation of CD4 cells.
source: Thus, the formation of RCS facilitated by IL-6 makes possible for this cytokine to sustain mitochondria hyperpolarization while minimizing the production of mROS during activation of CD4 cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased RCS and decreased mROS with IL-6 treatment.

claim: Despite the increased MMP, intracellular ATP levels were not affected by IL-6.
source: Surprisingly, despite of the increased MMP, intracellular ATP levels were not affected by IL-6 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATP measurement data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Analysis of ATP levels in culture supernatants of activated cells showed no difference in the levels of extracellular ATP.
source: However, analysis of ATP levels in culture supernatants of activated cells showed no difference in the levels of extracellular ATP (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by extracellular ATP measurement data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No statistically significant difference in basal mitochondrial OCR or maximal respiratory capacity was detected between cells activated with or without IL-6.
source: No statistically significant difference in basal mitochondrial OCR or maximal respiratory capacity was detected (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Seahorse OCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The effects of IL-6 on the MMP are uncoupled from OXPHOS.
source: Thus, the effects of IL-6 on the MMP are uncoupled from OXPHOS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased MMP but no change in ATP production or oxygen consumption.

claim: Lactate production was not significantly different in cells activated with IL-6.
source: Lactate production was not significantly different in cells activated with IL-6 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by lactate measurement data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There was no difference in anaerobic glycolysis in the presence of IL-6 during CD4 cell activation as measured by ECAR.
source: Consistent with the production of lactate, there was no difference in anaerobic glycolysis in the presence of IL-6 during CD4 cell activation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Seahorse ECAR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Although IL-6 maintains high MMP late during the activation of CD4 cells, it does not alter rates of OXPHOS or anaerobic glycolysis.
source: Thus, although IL-6 maintains high MMP late during the activation of CD4 cells, it does not alter rates of OXPHOS or anaerobic glycolysis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the metabolic data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake is modulated by mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and it is dictated by the MMP.
source: Mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake is modulated by mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU) and it is dictated by the MMP (Baughman et al., 2011; De Stefani et al., 2011; Mallilankaraman et al., 2012a, 2012b; Shanmughapriya et al., 2015), while Ca2+ release from mitochondria is mediated by the mitochondrial Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (mNCLX) (Kirichok et al., 2004; Palty et al., 2010; Nita et al., 2012; Rizzuto et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to established literature on mitochondrial calcium handling.

claim: There was a significantly greater frequency of cells with high levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ (Rhod-2high) in the presence of IL-6.
source: Consistent with an increased MMP, there was a significantly greater frequency of cells with high levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ (Rhod-2high) in the presence of IL-6 (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Rhod-2 flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A and 4C.

claim: Short treatment of IL-6-activated CD4 cells with CCCP significantly reduced the frequency of cells with high levels of mitochondrial Ca2+.
source: Short treatment of IL-6-activated CD4 cells with the depolarizing agent Carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazone (CCCP) significantly reduced the frequency of cells with high levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ (Rhod-2high) (Figure 4B,C), indicating that the increased levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ are dependent on mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and 4C using CCCP treatment.

claim: The increased levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ are dependent on mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
source: Short treatment of IL-6-activated CD4 cells with the depolarizing agent Carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazone (CCCP) significantly reduced the frequency of cells with high levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ (Rhod-2high) (Figure 4B,C), indicating that the increased levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ are dependent on mitochondrial hyperpolarization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CCCP treatment experiment showing that depolarization reduces mitochondrial Ca2+.

claim: The levels of cytosolic Ca2+ in cells activated with IL-6 were higher than in cells activated without IL-6.
source: The levels of cytosolic Ca2+, as determined by fluorometric ratio at 340 nm/380 nm (F340/380), in cells activated with IL-6 were higher than in cells activated without IL-6 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Fura-2 AM fluorometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Treatment with CGP-37157 lowered the cytosolic Ca2+ levels in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 to the levels found in those without IL-6.
source: Importantly, the treatment with CGP-37157, lowered the cytosolic Ca2+ levels in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 to the levels found in those without IL-6 (Figure 4D), indicating that this increase was dependent on mitochondrial Ca2+.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D using CGP-37157 treatment.

claim: The increase in cytosolic Ca2+ by IL-6 was dependent on mitochondrial Ca2+.
source: Importantly, the treatment with CGP-37157, lowered the cytosolic Ca2+ levels in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 to the levels found in those without IL-6 (Figure 4D), indicating that this increase was dependent on mitochondrial Ca2+.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the CGP-37157 treatment experiment.

claim: Reducing the MMP in IL-6-stimulated cells by treatment with inhibitors of Complex I (rotenone) and Complex III (antimycin) lowered the levels of cytosolic Ca2+.
source: In addition, reducing the MMP in IL-6-stimulated cells by treatment with inhibitors of Complex I (rotenone) and Complex III (antimycin) also lowered the levels of cytosolic Ca2+ (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D using rotenone and antimycin treatment.

claim: IL-6 provides a mechanism for CD4 cells to maintain elevated levels of cytosolic Ca2+ through its effect on the MMP and mitochondrial Ca2+.
source: IL-6 therefore provides a mechanism for CD4 cells to maintain elevated levels of cytosolic Ca2+ through its effect on the MMP and mitochondrial Ca2+.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing the relationship between IL-6, MMP, mitochondrial Ca2+, and cytosolic Ca2+.

claim: Several studies have shown the presence of Stat3 in mitochondria where it regulates the ETC primarily in tissues with high mitochondria content.
source: In addition to its role as a transcription factor, several studies have shown the presence of Stat3 in mitochondria where it regulates the ETC primarily in tissues with high mitochondria content (Gough et al., 2009; Wegrzyn et al., 2009; Heusch et al., 2011; Lachance et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2013; Erlich et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies on mitochondrial Stat3.

claim: Stat3 was present in both the nucleus and cytosol of activated CD4 cells.
source: As expected, Stat3 was present in both the nucleus and cytosol (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data of subcellular fractions shown in Figure 5A.

claim: High levels of Stat3 were present in mitochondria of activated CD4 cells.
source: Interestingly, however, high levels of Stat3 were also present in mitochondria (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data of mitochondrial fractions shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Only low levels of Stat3 were present in the mitochondrial fraction from freshly isolated CD4 cells.
source: Only low levels of Stat3 were present in the mitochondrial fraction from freshly isolated CD4 cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: High levels of Stat3 were detected in mitochondria from activated cells, but these levels were further upregulated by IL-6.
source: High levels of Stat3 were detected in mitochondria from activated cells, but these levels were further upregulated by IL-6 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: IL-6 did not have an effect on the total levels of Stat3 in whole cell lysates.
source: IL-6 did not have an effect on the total levels of Stat3 either, as determined by Western-blot using whole cell lysates (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: No phospho-Stat3 was detected in mitochondria from freshly isolated CD4 cells.
source: No phospho-Stat3 was detected in mitochondria from freshly isolated CD4 cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Phospho-Stat3 was present in mitochondria of activated CD4 cells, but the levels were substantially higher in the presence of IL-6.
source: Phospho-Stat3 was present in mitochondria of activated CD4 cells, but the levels were substantially higher in the presence of IL-6 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: IL-6 promotes the accumulation of Stat3 in mitochondria during CD4 cell activation.
source: Thus, IL-6 promotes the accumulation of Stat3 in mitochondria during CD4 cell activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Western blot data showing increased mitochondrial Stat3 with IL-6.

claim: IL-6 failed to increase MMP in Stat3-deficient CD4 cells during activation.
source: Interestingly, IL-6 failed to increase MMP in Stat3-deficient CD4 cells during activation (Figure 5D,E), indicating that effect of IL-6 on MMP in CD4 cells is dependent on Stat3.
evidence: This claim is supported by TMRE flow cytometry data in Stat3 knockout cells shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: The effect of IL-6 on MMP in CD4 cells is dependent on Stat3.
source: Interestingly, IL-6 failed to increase MMP in Stat3-deficient CD4 cells during activation (Figure 5D,E), indicating that effect of IL-6 on MMP in CD4 cells is dependent on Stat3.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experiment showing loss of IL-6 effect in Stat3-deficient cells.

claim: IL-6 was still able to increase MMP in CD4 cells from mut-Stat3 mice.
source: IL-6 was still able to increase MMP in CD4 cells from mut-Stat3 mice (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by TMRE flow cytometry data in mut-Stat3 cells shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The presence of Stattic did not affect the MMP in IL-6-treated CD4 cells.
source: The presence of Stattic, even at a relatively high concentration (Schust et al., 2006), did not affect the MMP in IL-6-treated CD4 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The increased MMP in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 requires Stat3, but it is independent of Stat3-mediated transcription.
source: Thus, correlating with the accumulation of Stat3 in mitochondria, the increased MMP in CD4 cells activated in the presence of IL-6 requires Stat3, but it is independent of Stat3-mediated transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experiments with mut-Stat3 and Stattic showing that transcriptional activity is not required.

claim: In the absence of Stat3, IL-6 failed to maintain elevated levels of mitochondrial Ca2+.
source: Interestingly, in the absence of Stat3, IL-6 failed to maintain elevated levels of mitochondrial Ca2+ (Figure 5G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by Rhod-2 flow cytometry data in Stat3 knockout cells shown in Figure 5G and 5H.

claim: IL-6 was capable to increase mitochondrial Ca2+ in mut-Stat3 CD4 cells.
source: Unlike Stat3 deficient CD4 cells, IL-6 was capable to increase mitochondrial Ca2+ in mut-Stat3 CD4 cells (Figure 5I,J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Rhod-2 flow cytometry data in mut-Stat3 cells shown in Figure 5I and 5J.

claim: IL-6 failed to increase cytosolic Ca2+ in Stat3−/− CD4 cells.
source: Unlike Stat3+/+ CD4 cells, IL-6 failed to increase cytosolic Ca2+ in Stat3−/− CD4 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by Fura-2 AM data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Stat3 contributes to mitochondrial Ca2+ in response to IL-6 and, consequently, cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis.
source: Together, these data show for the first time that Stat3 contributes to mitochondrial Ca2+ in response to IL-6 and, consequently, cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing Stat3 dependence of IL-6 effects on calcium.

claim: Previous studies have demonstrated the association of Stat3 with Complex I of the ETC through GRIM-19, a component of Complex I.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated the association of Stat3 with Complex I of the ETC through GRIM-19, a component of Complex I (Lufei et al., 2003; Gough et al., 2009; Wegrzyn et al., 2009; Tammineni et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on Stat3-GRIM-19 interaction.

claim: Stat3 was present in the SC region isolated from IL-6-treated CD4 cells.
source: Interestingly, Stat3 was also present in the SC region isolated from IL-6-treated CD4 cells (Figure 5K).
evidence: This claim is supported by BN-PAGE Western blot data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: Stat3 is recruited to the ETC SCs, where it can regulate activity of Complex I through interaction with GRIM-19.
source: Thus, Stat3 is recruited to the ETC SCs, where it can regulate activity of Complex I through interaction with GRIM-19.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing Stat3 presence in supercomplexes and known interactions with GRIM-19.

claim: IL-6, in the absence of other cytokines, is the major inducer of IL-21 production by CD4 cells in mouse and human.
source: IL-6, in the absence of other cytokines, is the major inducer of IL-21 production by CD4 cells in mouse and human (Nurieva et al., 2008; Suto et al., 2008; Dienz et al., 2009; Diehl et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nurieva et al., 2008; Suto et al., 2008; Dienz et al., 2009; Diehl et al., 2012.

claim: Stat3 is considered the main transcription factor that induces Il21 gene expression.
source: Stat3 is considered the main transcription factor that induces Il21 gene expression (Chen et al., 2006; Nurieva et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2007; Kaplan et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2006; Nurieva et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2007; Kaplan et al., 2011.

claim: IL-6 totally failed to induce IL-21 production in Stat3−/− CD4 cells.
source: Although IL-6 totally failed to induce IL-21 production in Stat3−/− CD4 cells (Figure 6A), it was able to trigger the production of IL-21 in mut-Stat3 CD4 cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: IL-6 was able to trigger the production of IL-21 in mut-Stat3 CD4 cells.
source: Although IL-6 totally failed to induce IL-21 production in Stat3−/− CD4 cells (Figure 6A), it was able to trigger the production of IL-21 in mut-Stat3 CD4 cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Stat3 can contribute to the production of IL-21 in response to IL-6 independently of its function of transcription factor.
source: Thus, correlating with its role on MMP and mitochondrial Ca2+, Stat3 can contribute to the production of IL-21 in response to IL-6 independently of its function of transcription factor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mut-Stat3 experiment showing IL-21 production without transcriptional activity.

claim: The increase in IL-21 levels late during activation was prevented by the treatment with R/A or CCCP.
source: However, the increase in IL-21 levels was prevented by the treatment with R/A or CCCP (Figure 6C), indicating that the late production of IL-21 was dependent on the increased MMP caused by IL-6.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The late production of IL-21 was dependent on the increased MMP caused by IL-6.
source: However, the increase in IL-21 levels was prevented by the treatment with R/A or CCCP (Figure 6C), indicating that the late production of IL-21 was dependent on the increased MMP caused by IL-6.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effect of depolarizing agents on IL-21 production.

claim: The increase in IL-21 production was prevented by CGP-37157.
source: The increase in IL-21 production was also prevented by CGP-37157 (Figure 6C), showing that the increased mitochondrial Ca2+ elicited by IL-6 also contributes to the late production of IL-21.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The increased mitochondrial Ca2+ elicited by IL-6 contributes to the late production of IL-21.
source: The increase in IL-21 production was also prevented by CGP-37157 (Figure 6C), showing that the increased mitochondrial Ca2+ elicited by IL-6 also contributes to the late production of IL-21.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effect of CGP-37157 on IL-21 production.

claim: The levels of IL-4 were increased in the last 6 hr in IL-6-stimulated CD4 cells, however R/A, CCCP or CGP-37157 prevented this increase.
source: Similar to IL-21, the levels of IL-4 were increased in the last 6 hr in IL-6-stimulated CD4 cells, however R/A, CCCP or CGP-37157 prevented this increase (Figure 6D), indicating that the increased MMP and cytosolic Ca2+ regulated by mitochondrial Ca2+ caused by IL-6 also contributes to the late production of IL-4.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The increased MMP and cytosolic Ca2+ regulated by mitochondrial Ca2+ caused by IL-6 contributes to the late production of IL-4.
source: Similar to IL-21, the levels of IL-4 were increased in the last 6 hr in IL-6-stimulated CD4 cells, however R/A, CCCP or CGP-37157 prevented this increase (Figure 6D), indicating that the increased MMP and cytosolic Ca2+ regulated by mitochondrial Ca2+ caused by IL-6 also contributes to the late production of IL-4.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the effect of mitochondrial inhibitors on IL-4 production.

claim: IL-6 had no effect on IL-2 production and treatment with R/A, CCCP or CGP-37157 had no effect on IL-2.
source: In contrast, IL-6 had no effect on IL-2 production and treatment with R/A, CCCP or CGP-37157 had no effect (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6E.
